about.title: Walnut Creek Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Walnut Creek's workforce spans downtown offices along N Main Street, medical and retail jobs near Treat Boulevard, and the crews who keep construction sites and delivery routes moving across Contra Costa County. When someone is hurt on the clock here, the first question is usually about workers' compensation, and that system does cover most on-the-job injuries no matter who was at fault. It is also, in most cases, the only claim you can bring against your own employer. What many people in Walnut Creek do not realize is that a separate injury claim may exist when a third party caused the harm: a subcontractor on a shared site, a property owner who ignored a hazard, the maker of a faulty tool, or another driver. That last one matters in a city where working trips run daily along I-680 and Ygnacio Valley Road, and where 2025 public records logged 310 injury collisions and 413 people injured. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can review both paths.

items.question: I was hit on I-680 while driving for my job in Walnut Creek. Is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. If you were working at the time, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of who caused the crash. If another driver was at fault, though, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver, which is a common situation on commuter corridors like I-680 and Ygnacio Valley Road. An attorney can evaluate both so nothing is left on the table.

items.question: My employer is hinting I should not file a claim. What can I do?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a work injury or filing for workers' compensation. Report the injury in writing within 30 days so there is a clear record. If you are being pressured, that is worth mentioning to the attorney you are connected with, because it can affect how your case is handled.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim against a third party in Contra Costa County?
items.answer: For most third-party personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. Workers' compensation has its own separate reporting rules, starting with the 30-day notice to your employer. Because these timelines run at the same time, it helps to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.
